definition: Training a model to refuse or redirect harmful requests, and across 7 sources a problem the archive's reasoning-model material reframes as being about structure rather than about refusal behaviour. Two sources make the same argument from different directions: one attributes reasoning models' safety failures to the reasoning structure itself and achieves alignment by altering that structure with 1,000 supervised examples and no reinforcement learning; another supervises the mechanism of a successful attack -- unmask the intent, explain how the syntax concealed it, derive the defence -- and finds that pairing the same jailbreaks with the teacher's refusal alone moves average attack success by 4 points against the analysis's 60. The corpus's recurring measurements: pattern-keyed alignment fails to transfer to unseen syntax, with one defence leaving gradient-optimised suffix attacks at the base model's rate; the utility cost is family-dependent and attributed to reasoning-style mismatch with the teacher rather than to safety training as such; and the whole evaluation is judge-mediated, with one paper's own audit finding two judges disagreeing on 42 percent of the class that determines the score. One archived method reduces harmful completions from 13.8 to 4.1 percent while gaining helpfulness, which is the archive's evidence that the safety tax is not inevitable.

evidence.note: Triggers a safety intervention in image diffusion from the intermediate clean-image estimate rather than from the prompt, and spends optimization only from the first timestep where a violation actually appears — so extra test-time compute is incurred on unsafe inputs and benign latency stays flat as the budget grows.
evidence.title: Test-Time Scaling for Safe Text-Guided Image Generation via Intermediate Clean Estimates

evidence.note: Tampers with a model's own reasoning trace in two directions — toward an equivalent safe option and toward an unsafe one — and finds the models that follow their traces most faithfully are the ones that follow them into harm, with the two behaviours carried by two distinct, anti-correlated residual-stream directions that can be steered apart.
evidence.title: Risky Business: Measuring The Faithfulness-Safety Tension

evidence.note: Compresses a safety guard's textual rationales into continuous latent states by a staged curriculum, cutting 268 reasoning tokens to 1.60 and latency 8.9-fold, and adds an on-demand decoder that reconstructs a human-readable audit artifact — whose own ablation shows the artifact is anchored far more by the source text than by the latent states it is supposed to inspect.
evidence.title: LatentGuard: Efficient and Inspectable Latent Reasoning for LLM Safeguards

evidence.note: Builds safety-alignment training data by first having an agent jailbreak a strong teacher and only then asking that teacher to explain why the successful attack worked, so the student is supervised on the mechanism of the attack rather than on the refusal.
evidence.title: Dual-Adversarial Safety Alignment: Cultivating Intrinsic Threat Comprehension in LRMs

evidence.note: Argues reasoning models' safety failures come from the reasoning structure itself, and achieves safety alignment by altering that structure with 1K supervised examples and no RL.
evidence.title: Reasoning Structure Matters for Safety Alignment of Reasoning Models

evidence.note: Names Self-Jailbreak, where a model correctly flags a query as harmful and then overrides that judgement during later reasoning steps, and intervenes step-wise rather than over whole trajectories.
evidence.title: When Models Outthink Their Safety: Unveiling and Mitigating Self-Jailbreak in Large Reasoning Models

evidence.note: Adds a Self-Reflection token that lets reasoning models recover from harmful output mid-generation, cutting harmful completion rate from 13.8% to 4.1%.
evidence.title: Self-Reflection Improves Safety of Large Reasoning Models

name: safety alignment
